title: `m ∣ n → fib m ∣ fib n` is one law, proved separately over ℕ and over ℤ
claim: Both facts say the Fibonacci sequence is divisibility-monotone: the index dividing implies the term dividing. Erasing the carrier leaves the identical string `∀ (m n : ⟨C⟩), m ∣ n → ⟨C⟩.fib m ∣ ⟨C⟩.fib n` on both sides. The two proofs are unrelated in the ledger — the ℕ one goes through `Nat.fib_gcd` and the ℤ one has no recorded dependency at all — so no dependency edge connects them and none ever will if the ℤ proof stays direct.
transport: The same cast as the vanishing law: `Int.fib ↑n = ↑(Nat.fib n)` on nonnegative arguments, `Int.fib (-n) = ±Int.fib n` on the rest, and the fact that `↑a ∣ ↑b` and `a ∣ b` agree under `Int.ofNat`.

via.step: Int.fib agrees with Nat.fib on the image of the nonnegative cast, so the ℕ statement transports onto 0 ≤ m, n
Int.fib on a negative argument is ±Int.fib of its absolute value, and divisibility is insensitive to sign
Divisibility is preserved and reflected by Int.ofNat — `↑a ∣ ↑b ↔ a ∣ b`. This is the step the transport turns on and the ledger does not state it

provenance.established_by: lane agent-correspondence-model (2026-08-24), from the committed formal statements and the ledger's `depends_on` closure.

notes: Worth noting what the carrier erasure does NOT check: it compares statements, not proofs, so it can only say the two facts assert the same law. It cannot say the ℤ proof is a transport of the ℕ one, and here it very likely is not — the ℕ proof factors through `Nat.fib_gcd` and the ℤ fact records no dependency at all. That asymmetry is exactly why `derivation_status` is a separate axis from the structural check: the check is what makes the pairing honest, the axis is what stops it being read as a derivation.
